tagline: OV-099 — second operational Shuttle. Lost 73s after launch on STS-51-L (1986-01-28) with all seven crew including teacher Christa McAuliffe
description: Built from a structural test article (STA-099) converted to flight after Enterprise was deemed too expensive to upgrade. First flew STS-6 (1983-04-04) carrying out the first Shuttle EVA. 10 missions before STS-51-L (1986-01-28) launched at unprecedented cold (−1 °C) — the right SRB's O-rings failed to seal, hot gas burned through the strut attaching the SRB to the external tank, and the orbiter broke apart at Max-Q (T+73s) at 14 km altitude. All seven crew perished. The Rogers Commission ground the Shuttle for 32 months and rewrote NASA's safety culture.
best_known_for: Second Shuttle; lost 73s after launch on STS-51-L 1986-01-28 with 7 crew
